title: Manual handling of heavy appliances and equipment
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: Safe Work Australia, Hazardous manual tasks (model code of practice) (no date shown; publication date field blank); legislation.gov.au, Work Health and Safety (Hazardous Manual Tasks) Code of Practice 2015 (approval signed 18 March 2016 per the text; no page date shown).
audience: Workers who move, tilt, slide or reposition heavy appliances, trays and equipment for cleaning, including commercial dishwashers, ovens, fryers, ice machines and laundry machines
learningOutcomes: Assess the weight, shape and handling points of an appliance before moving it
Plan a move using the right equipment, team size and route
Identify the hidden hazards of moving an appliance, such as leads, hoses and drains
Decide when a move is outside the safe limit and must be referred

instruction.heading: Why moving an appliance is a risk of its own
instruction.body: Moving a machine to clean behind it is one of the most common causes of back and joint injury on appliance jobs. The weight of a commercial dishwasher, oven or ice machine can be far above what one person can lift safely, and the weight is often poorly placed, with the centre of gravity high or to one side. Appliances also have sharp corners, exposed fittings, hoses and leads that can catch, and their feet or castors may not roll on the floor where you need them to. Moving a machine can also disconnect a hose or lead, damage a drain, or cause a fitting to leak. The Safe Work Australia model code on hazardous manual tasks requires these risks to be assessed and managed, and it aims at removing or reducing them (no page date shown). The page does not list weight or posture factors. A machine that does not need to be moved should not be moved.

instruction.heading: Plan the move before you lift
instruction.body: Before you move any appliance, check its weight from the manufacturer's specification or the data plate, and compare it with the team size and equipment on site. If the appliance cannot be moved safely by the team available, do not attempt it. Check the route for steps, thresholds, ramps, wet or greasy floors, narrow doorways, and obstacles. Identify the handling points that the manufacturer allows, which are usually the base or designated lifting points, and avoid lifting by panels, doors, handles or control housings, because they can bend or break. Disconnect nothing without isolation under lesson “Making a machine safe before cleaning: isolation, stored energy and moving parts”. Check for leads, hoses and drain lines that will become stretched, and check whether the site has a trolley or a platform truck suited to the load. Agree the signal and the direction of travel with your team before you start, so that everyone moves together.

instruction.heading: Moving, positioning and returning the machine
instruction.body: Keep the load close to the body, bend the knees, keep the back straight and avoid twisting while lifting. Tilt a machine only when the manufacturer allows it, and only by the method the manufacturer sets out, because tilting can move oil, water, or internal parts. Slide a machine on a sheet or a board where the floor is hard and the machine's base allows it, rather than dragging it across the floor. Keep feet clear of the path and stop if the load shifts. Set the machine down on a level floor, and check that the castors lock and that the machine is stable before you leave it. When you return the machine to its position, check that all leads and hoses are free and not crushed, that the drain is clear, and that the machine sits level. Do not move a machine with an oven door open, a drawer out or a fryer holding oil.

procedure: Check the appliance's weight and lifting points from the manufacturer's specification or data plate, and record them.
Compare the weight with the team and equipment available. If the move is beyond the safe limit, stop and refer.
Isolate the appliance and disconnect nothing without the isolation step in “Making a machine safe before cleaning: isolation, stored energy and moving parts” and the manufacturer's sequence.
Walk the route, noting steps, thresholds, wet floors, narrow doors and hazards.
Clear the route and put down protection on the floor where a board or sheet is used.
Agree the signal and direction with your team, then lift or slide together using the approved lifting points.
Set the machine down on a level floor, lock the castors, and check stability before leaving it.
Check all leads, hoses and drain lines after the move, and record any damage found.

workedExamples.situation: A commercial dishwasher must be pulled out from under the bench to clean behind it. You are alone. The machine is heavy, has a water inlet hose and a drain hose, and the floor is wet from the last job.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you pull the machine out alone?
workedExamples.reasoning: A heavy machine with hoses on a wet floor is not a one-person move. Do not pull it out alone. Ask for a second person or the equipment the site provides. Isolate the machine first, check the weight, and dry the floor before the move. Do not disconnect the hoses without the manufacturer's sequence. If the team cannot move it safely, refer the cleaning behind the machine to the owner.

workedExamples.situation: A commercial ice machine has to be moved 2 metres to clean the wall behind it. The front panel handle looks loose.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Where do you grip the machine?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not lift by the loose handle or the front panel, because these are not rated handling points and can detach. Use the manufacturer's lifting points or the base where the design allows it. If there are no clear points, use a trolley or platform truck the site provides, and report the loose handle to the site contact.

equipmentAndPpe: Platform trolley or sack truck rated for the load, where the site provides one
Protective sheet or board for sliding machines on hard floors
Safety footwear, gloves with grip, and back-support practice as set by the business
Non-slip mats or floor signs for wet areas

commonErrors.error: Lifting an appliance by a loose handle, door or control panel.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only the manufacturer's lifting points or the base, and use a trolley where the points are unclear.

commonErrors.error: Moving a machine that is still connected to a hose, lead or drain.
commonErrors.prevention: Isolate and follow the manufacturer's disconnection sequence before any move. Check all connections after.

commonErrors.error: Moving a fryer or other appliance while it still contains oil or hot water.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the appliance is cool and empty according to the site procedure before moving it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The Safe Work Australia model code on hazardous manual tasks says manual tasks must be assessed and managed. Work to the assessment in the business procedure.
The Work Health and Safety (Hazardous Manual Tasks) Code of Practice 2015 was approved on 18 March 2016 and is held on legislation.gov.au.

Lifting or moving equipment that is part of a fixed installation, or work that involves disconnecting a gas or electrical connection, is regulated work and is outside this lesson. This lesson does not grant a licence for that work.

qualityStandard: The weight and lifting points are checked before any move, and the move is within the team's capability
The appliance is isolated and any connections are handled as the manufacturer sets out
The machine is returned to a level, stable position with leads, hoses and drains free and undamaged
documentationEvidence: The weight and lifting point record for each appliance moved
The record of any move that was refused or referred, and the reason
The check of leads, hoses and drains after the move, with any damage found
summary: Moving an appliance is a manual task with its own hazards, and the first control is not moving it at all.
Plan the move, check the weight and lifting points, isolate, and agree the team's signals before you lift.
After the move, check leads, hoses and drains, and record any damage.

knowledgeChecks.question: A commercial dishwasher is to be moved for cleaning behind it. You are alone and the machine has water and drain hoses connected. What is the correct action?
options: Cut the hoses so the machine moves more easily across the floor without needing a second person or equipment
Ask the customer to lift one side while you pull the other, since that is quicker than fetching a trolley
Pull it out alone while the hoses are still attached, to save time, since the hoses will stretch enough
Isolate it, arrange a second person or suitable equipment, and do not disconnect hoses outside the manufacturer's sequence

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should you lift an appliance from?
options: By the manufacturer's lifting points or the base where the design allows it
By a loose front handle, because it is the easiest grip to reach from the floor
By the door, which is strong enough to carry the weight of the whole machine
By the control panel, which is fixed to the frame and can take the load

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the first control for a manual handling risk on an appliance job?
options: Wearing the thickest gloves available, since grip matters most on the job
Avoiding the manual task where the machine does not need to be moved
Lifting faster to reduce the time the load is held by the worker
Moving the machine while it is still running, so the job is finished sooner

knowledgeChecks.question: After you move a machine back into position, what should you check?
options: Only whether the machine looks straight against the wall from where you are standing
Whether the customer is happy with the position of the machine after the move is done
That leads, hoses and drain lines are free and undamaged, and the machine is level and stable
Only the colour of the control panel, since the panel shows the status of the machine

knowledgeChecks.question: When must a move be stopped and referred?
options: Only when the customer has asked for it in writing, even if the team is uncertain
Never, because teams can always lift more together than one person alone, so no move is ever stopped
Only when the appliance is switched on, since the power then shows whether the load is too heavy
When the appliance weight is beyond what the team can move safely with the equipment available
